title.en: Volume 92: Notable Women - Cui Lan's Consort Feng, Feng Zhuo's Consort Liu, Wei Pu's Consort Fang, Hu Changming's Consort Zhang
title.raw: 卷92 列女:崔覧妻封氏 封卓妻劉氏 魏溥妻房氏 胡長命妻張氏 Volume 92: Notable Women - Cui Lan's Consort Feng, Feng Zhuo's Consort Liu, Wei Pu's Consort Fang, Hu Changming's Consort Zhang

sentences.zh: 崔覽妻封氏 封卓妻劉氏 魏溥妻房氏 胡長命妻張氏 平原女子孫氏 房愛親妻崔氏 涇州貞女兕先氏[1] 姚氏婦楊氏 張洪初妻劉氏[2] 董景起妻張氏 陽尼妻高氏 史映周妻耿氏 任城國太妃孟氏 苟金龍妻劉氏 盧元禮妻李氏 河東孝女姚氏 刁思遵妻魯氏

translations.literal: Cui Lan's wife Lady Feng; Feng Zhuo's wife Lady Liu; Wei Pu's wife Lady Fang; Hu Changming's wife Lady Zhang; the woman Sun of Pingyuan; Fang Aiqin's wife Lady Cui; the chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture; Lady Yang, daughter-in-law of the Yao clan; Zhang Hongchu's wife Lady Liu; Dong Jingqi's wife Lady Zhang; Yang Ni's wife Lady Gao; Shi Yingzhou's wife Lady Geng; Grand Consort Meng of the State of Rencheng; Gou Jinlong's wife Lady Liu; Lu Yuanli's wife Lady Li; the filial daughter Yao of Hedong; Diao Sizun's wife Lady Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng, consort of Cui Lan; Lady Liu, consort of Feng Zhuo; Lady Fang, consort of Wei Pu; Lady Zhang, consort of Hu Changming; Sun Nanyu of Pingyuan; Lady Cui, consort of Fang Aiqin; the chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture; Lady Yang of the Yao household; Lady Liu, consort of Zhang Hongchu; Lady Zhang, consort of Dong Jingqi; Lady Gao, consort of Yang Ni; Lady Geng, consort of Shi Yingzhou; Grand Consort Meng of Rencheng; Lady Liu, consort of Gou Jinlong; Lady Li, consort of Lu Yuanli; the filial daughter Yao of Hedong; Lady Lu, consort of Diao Sizun.

sentences.zh: 夫婦人之事，存於織絍組紃、酒漿醯醢而已。

translations.literal: As for the affairs of married women, they consist merely in weaving, spinning, cords, wine, vinegar, and pickled foods.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinarily, a married woman's duties extend no further than weaving, spinning, cord-making, and preparing wine, vinegar, and preserves.

sentences.zh: 至如嫫訓軒宮，娥成舜業，塗山三母，克昌二邦，殆非匹婦之謂也。

translations.literal: As for Mo instructing in the Xuan Palace, E completing Shun's enterprise, and the three mothers of Tushan bringing prosperity to two states—these are scarcely what one calls ordinary wives.
translations.idiomatic: Cases such as Mo instructing in the Xuan Palace, E completing Shun's work, and the three mothers of Tushan bringing two realms to flourish scarcely belong to the category of ordinary wives.

sentences.zh: 若乃明識列操，文辯兼該，聲自閨庭，號顯列國，子政集之於前，元凱編之於後，隨時綴錄，代不乏人。

translations.literal: When it comes to those with clear understanding of principle and conduct, accomplished in both literary and argumentative skill, whose reputation arose from within the women's quarters and whose fame was manifest across the states—Liu Xiang gathered them in former times, Yuan Kai compiled them afterward, recording them according to the times; each age has not lacked such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are women of clear moral insight and conduct, equally skilled in letters and debate, whose renown rose from the inner quarters and whose names shone across the realm. Liu Xiang collected such figures in earlier times, and Yuan Kai compiled them afterward, recording them age by age—no generation has lacked them.

sentences.zh: 今書魏世可知者為列女傳。

translations.literal: In this book, those known from Wei times are recorded as biographies of exemplary women.
translations.idiomatic: This volume records those exemplary women known from the Wei period.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎清河崔覽妻封氏，勃海人，散騎常侍愷女也。

translations.literal: Lady Feng, wife of Cui Lan, Secretariat Gentleman of Qinghe, was a native of Bohai and daughter of the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng, consort of Cui Lan, Secretariat Gentleman of Qinghe, came from Bohai and was the daughter of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Kai.

sentences.zh: 有才識，聰辯強記，多所究知，於時婦人莫能及。

translations.literal: She had talent and insight, was clever, eloquent, and possessed a strong memory, and had investigated and learned many things; among women of the time none could match her.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and discerning, quick-witted, eloquent, and possessed of a formidable memory, she had mastered a wide range of learning—no woman of her day could equal her.

sentences.zh: 李敷、公孫文叔雖已貴重，近世故事有所不達，皆就而諮請焉。

translations.literal: Although Li Fu and Gongsun Wenshu were already eminent and honored, whenever there were recent precedents they did not understand, they all came to consult her.
translations.idiomatic: Even men as eminent as Li Fu and Gongsun Wenshu would seek her out whenever they were uncertain about recent precedents.

sentences.zh: 勃海封卓妻，彭城劉氏女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Feng Zhuo of Bohai was a daughter of the Liu clan of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Feng Zhuo of Bohai was a daughter of the Liu clan of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 成婚一夕，卓官於京師，後以事伏法。

translations.literal: One night after their marriage, Zhuo was serving in office at the capital; later he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: They had been married only one night when Zhuo took office in the capital; he was later executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 劉氏在家，忽然夢想，知卓已死，哀泣不輟。

translations.literal: Liu remained at home and suddenly dreamed; she knew Zhuo was already dead and wept in grief without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Liu remained at home when she was suddenly visited by a dream and knew that Zhuo was dead; she wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 諸嫂喻之不止，經旬，凶問果至，遂憤歎而死。

translations.literal: Her sisters-in-law admonished her repeatedly without stopping her; after ten days the news of death indeed arrived, and she died in grief and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Her sisters-in-law tried in vain to console her; ten days later the news of his death arrived, and she died of grief.

sentences.zh: 時人比之秦嘉妻。

translations.literal: People of the time compared her to the wife of Qin Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries compared her to the wife of Qin Jia.

sentences.zh: 中書令高允念其義高而名不著，為之詩曰：「兩儀正位，人倫肇甄。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun, mindful that her righteousness was lofty yet her name was not renowned, composed a poem for her, saying: "Heaven and earth hold their proper places; human relations are first distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun, reflecting that her virtue was lofty yet her name obscure, composed a poem for her that begins: "Heaven and earth hold their stations; human bonds take their first form.

sentences.zh: 爰制夫婦，統業承先。

translations.literal: Thus husband and wife were instituted to carry on the ancestral enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus were husband and wife ordained to carry on the work of their forebears.

sentences.zh: 雖曰異族，氣猶自然。

translations.literal: Though called different clans, their vital affinities remain natural.
translations.idiomatic: Though called different clans, their spirits remain naturally joined.

sentences.zh: 生則同室，終契黃泉。

translations.literal: In life they share one chamber; in death they pledge themselves in the yellow springs.
translations.idiomatic: In life they share one roof; in death they are pledged in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 〈其一〉

translations.literal: 〈Part One〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part One〉

sentences.zh: 封生令達，卓為時彥。

translations.literal: Feng was born accomplished and penetrating; Zhuo was a worthy man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was born gifted and discerning; Zhuo was a leading man of his time.

sentences.zh: 內協黃中，外兼三變。

translations.literal: Within he harmonized with the yellow center; without he mastered the three transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Within he embodied the golden mean; without he mastered the three changes.

sentences.zh: 誰能作配，克應其選。

translations.literal: Who could be his match? She fully answered to the choice.
translations.idiomatic: Who could be his equal? She alone met that standard.

sentences.zh: 實有華宗，挺生淑媛。

translations.literal: Truly there was a splendid clan, from which arose this virtuous lady.
translations.idiomatic: From a noble house she rose, a lady of rare grace.

sentences.zh: 〈其二〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Two〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Two〉

sentences.zh: 京野勢殊，山川乖互。

translations.literal: The capital and the countryside differed in circumstance; mountains and rivers stood apart.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and countryside lay far apart; mountains and rivers divided them.

sentences.zh: 乃奉王命，載馳在路。

translations.literal: Then he received the king's command and hurried along the road.
translations.idiomatic: He received the royal command and sped along the road.

sentences.zh: 公務既弘，私義獲著。

translations.literal: Public duty being already broad, private obligation was thereby fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: His public duties widened, yet private obligation was honored.

sentences.zh: 因媒致幣，遘止一暮。

translations.literal: Through a go-between betrothal gifts were sent, and they met and stayed but one evening.
translations.idiomatic: Through a matchmaker betrothal gifts were exchanged, and they shared but a single evening.

sentences.zh: 〈其三〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Three〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Three〉

sentences.zh: 率我初冠，眷彼弱笄。

translations.literal: I had just donned my first cap; she cherished her tender hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: I had just come of age; she wore her maiden hairpin.

sentences.zh: 形由禮比，情以趣諧。

translations.literal: Their forms were matched by ritual; their feelings were joined by inclination.
translations.idiomatic: Rite bound their forms together; inclination drew their hearts as one.

sentences.zh: 忻願難常，影跡易乖。

translations.literal: Joyful wishes are hard to keep constant; shadow and footprint are easily parted.
translations.idiomatic: Joy is hard to hold; shadow and footprint part all too soon.

sentences.zh: 悠悠言邁，戚戚長懷。

translations.literal: Far stretches the journey of words; long and sorrowful is the heart's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Words stretch into the distance; grief lodges in the heart.

sentences.zh: 〈其四〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Four〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Four〉

sentences.zh: 時值險屯，橫離塵網。

translations.literal: The time met with peril and hardship; he was torn from the dusty net of life.
translations.idiomatic: Hard times came; he was torn from the web of mortal life.

sentences.zh: 伏鑕就刑，身分土壤。

translations.literal: He submitted to the blade and underwent punishment; body and self returned to the soil.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to the blade; body and self returned to earth.

sentences.zh: 千里雖遐，應如影響。

translations.literal: Though a thousand li were distant, she responded like shadow to sound.
translations.idiomatic: Though a thousand li lay between them, she answered like shadow to echo.

sentences.zh: 良嬪洞感，發於夢想。

translations.literal: The good consort perceived deeply and was stirred, arising from a dream.
translations.idiomatic: The faithful bride felt it in her depths and knew it in a dream.

sentences.zh: 〈其五〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Five〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Five〉

sentences.zh: 仰惟親命，俯尋嘉好。

translations.literal: Looking up she considered her parents' command; looking down she sought their fine match.
translations.idiomatic: She honored her parents' charge above and cherished their fine match below.

sentences.zh: 誰謂會淺，義深情到。

translations.literal: Who would say their meeting was shallow? In righteousness her feeling ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: Who could call their meeting brief? Duty bound her, and love ran deep.

sentences.zh: 畢志守窮，誓不二醮。

translations.literal: She fulfilled her resolve and kept to her widowhood, vowing never to marry again.
translations.idiomatic: She held to her purpose in widowhood, vowing never to take another husband.

sentences.zh: 何以驗之？

translations.literal: How may this be verified?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be proved?

sentences.zh: 殞身是効。

translations.literal: She gave up her life as proof.
translations.idiomatic: She gave her life as proof.

sentences.zh: 〈其六〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Six〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Six〉

sentences.zh: 人之處世，孰不厚生。

translations.literal: Among those who dwell in the world, who does not cherish life?
translations.idiomatic: Who among the living does not cherish life?

sentences.zh: 必存於義，所重則輕。

translations.literal: She held fast to righteousness; what others valued she held light.
translations.idiomatic: She held to righteousness and made light of what others prized.

sentences.zh: 結忿鍾心，甘就幽冥。

translations.literal: Grievance gathered in her heart; she willingly entered the dark underworld.
translations.idiomatic: Grief lodged in her heart; she willingly entered the shades.

sentences.zh: 永捐堂宇，長辭母兄。

translations.literal: Forever she abandoned the hall and chambers; long she bade farewell to mother and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Forever she left the hall and home; long she bade farewell to mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 〈其七〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Seven〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Seven〉

sentences.zh: 茫茫中野，翳翳孤丘。

translations.literal: Vast is the central wild; dim is the lonely mound.
translations.idiomatic: Vast lies the open wild; dim stands the lonely mound.

sentences.zh: 葛虆冥蒙，荊棘四周。

translations.literal: Kudzu and brambles lie dark and tangled; thorns and brambles surround it on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Kudzu and brambles lie dark and tangled; thorns ring it on every side.

sentences.zh: 理苟不昧，神必俱游。

translations.literal: If principle is not obscured, spirits will surely wander together.
translations.idiomatic: If truth is not dimmed, their spirits will wander together still.

sentences.zh: 異哉貞婦，曠世靡疇。」

translations.literal: How extraordinary is this chaste wife—throughout the ages without peer."
translations.idiomatic: How rare this faithful wife—without equal in any age."

sentences.zh: 〈其八〉

translations.literal: 〈Part Eight〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Part Eight〉

sentences.zh: 鉅鹿魏溥妻，常山房氏女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Pu of Julu was a daughter of the Fang clan of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Wei Pu of Julu was a daughter of the Fang clan of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 父堪，慕容垂貴鄉太守。

translations.literal: Her father Kan was Administrator of Guixiang under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Kan served as Administrator of Guixiang under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 房氏婉順高明，幼有烈操。

translations.literal: Lady Fang was gentle, compliant, lofty, and clear-minded, and from youth possessed a fierce integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fang was gentle, compliant, and of lofty character; from childhood she possessed a resolute integrity.

sentences.zh: 年十六而溥遇病且卒，顧謂之曰：「人生如白駒過隙，死不足恨，但夙心往志，不聞於沒世矣。

translations.literal: At age sixteen Pu fell ill and was about to die; he turned to her and said: "Human life is like a white colt passing a crack—death is not worth regretting, but my long-cherished heart and former aspirations will not be heard of after my passing.
translations.idiomatic: When she was sixteen, Pu fell mortally ill and said to her: "Life passes like a white colt through a crack—death itself is no grief, but the hopes I have cherished all my life will die unheard.

sentences.zh: 良痛母老家貧，供奉無寄；

translations.literal: I truly grieve that my mother is old and the household poor, with no one to provide support;
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that my mother is old, our household poor, and no one left to support her;

sentences.zh: 赤子矇眇，血祀孤危。

translations.literal: the infant child is blind and helpless; the blood sacrifices stand alone in peril.
translations.idiomatic: our infant son is helpless, and the ancestral line stands in peril.

sentences.zh: 所以抱怨於黃墟耳。

translations.literal: this is why I lodge my complaint in the yellow mound."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I lodge my complaint in the grave."

sentences.zh: 」[4]房垂泣而對曰：「幸承先人餘訓，出事君子，義在自畢。

translations.literal: [4] Fang wept as she replied: "Fortunately I have received the leftover teachings of my forebears; having gone forth to serve a gentleman, righteousness lies in fulfilling it to the end.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Fang wept as she answered: "I have been fortunate to receive my ancestors' teaching; having married a gentleman, my duty is to see it through to the end.

sentences.zh: 有志不從，命也。

translations.literal: To have the will yet not follow through—this is fate.
translations.idiomatic: To have the will yet fail to fulfill it—that is fate.

sentences.zh: 夫人在堂，稚子襁褓，顧當以身少，相感長往之恨。

translations.literal: Your mother is in the hall and the young child is in swaddling clothes; I should, considering that I am younger, share in the long grief of your departure.
translations.idiomatic: Your mother is still in the hall and our child still in swaddling clothes; though I am young, I shall bear the burden of your long absence.

sentences.zh: 」[5]俄而溥卒。

translations.literal: [5] Shortly afterward Pu died.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Shortly afterward Pu died.

sentences.zh: 及大斂，房氏操刀割左耳，投之棺中，仍曰：「鬼神有知，相期泉壤。

translations.literal: At the grand encoffinment, Lady Fang took a knife, cut off her left ear, and cast it into the coffin, saying: "If spirits have knowledge, let us meet in the springs and soil.
translations.idiomatic: At the encoffinment, Lady Fang took a knife, cut off her left ear, and cast it into the coffin, saying: "If the spirits have knowledge, let us meet in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 」流血滂然，助喪者咸皆哀懼。

translations.literal: " Blood flowed profusely; all who assisted at the funeral were moved to grief and fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Blood poured forth, and all who attended the funeral were stricken with grief and awe.

sentences.zh: 姑劉氏輟哭而謂曰：「新婦何至於此！

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law, Lady Liu, stopped weeping and said: "New bride, how could you go so far!
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Lady Liu stopped weeping and said, "Daughter-in-law, how could you go so far!

sentences.zh: 」房對曰：「新婦少年不幸，[6]實慮父母未量至情，覬持此自誓耳。

translations.literal: " Fang replied: "The new bride met misfortune in her youth; [6] I truly feared my parents would not gauge the depth of my feeling and hoped to hold this as a pledge to myself.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang answered, "Your daughter-in-law met misfortune young; [6] I feared my parents would not grasp the depth of my devotion and meant this act as a pledge to myself.

sentences.zh: 」聞知者莫不感愴。

translations.literal: " All who heard were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: " All who heard were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 於時子緝生未十旬，鞠育於後房之內，未曾出門。

translations.literal: At that time her son Ji was not yet ten days old; she reared him within the inner chambers and never went out the door.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Ji was then less than ten days old; she reared him within the inner quarters and never once left the house.

sentences.zh: 遂終身不聽絲竹，不預座席。

translations.literal: Thereafter for her whole life she would not listen to string and bamboo music or take part in seated gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of her life she would not listen to music or take her place at a feast.

sentences.zh: 緝年十二，房父母仍存，於是歸寧。

translations.literal: When Ji was twelve, Fang's parents were still alive, and she therefore returned for a visit home.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was twelve and Fang's parents were still living, she made a visit home.

sentences.zh: 父兄尚有異議，緝竊聞之，以啟母。

translations.literal: Her father and brothers still had reservations; Ji overheard this privately and reported it to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her father and brothers still had doubts about her resolve; Ji overheard them and told his mother.

sentences.zh: 房命駕紿云他行，因而遂歸，其家弗知之也。

translations.literal: Fang ordered the carriage harnessed and falsely said she was going elsewhere; thus she returned home, and her family did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang ordered the carriage prepared, pretended she was bound elsewhere, and returned home before her family realized what she had heard.

sentences.zh: 行數十里方覺，兄弟來追，房哀歎而不反。

translations.literal: After traveling several tens of li they noticed; her brothers came in pursuit, but Fang lamented and would not return.
translations.idiomatic: After several tens of li her family realized what had happened and her brothers came in pursuit, but Fang wept and would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 其執意如此。

translations.literal: Such was the firmness of her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the firmness of her purpose.

sentences.zh: 訓導一子，有母儀法度。

translations.literal: She instructed and guided one son, possessing the demeanor and standards of a mother.
translations.idiomatic: She raised one son with the bearing and discipline of a true mother.

sentences.zh: 緝所交游有名勝者，則身具酒飯；

translations.literal: When Ji's associates included men of renown and distinction, she personally prepared wine and food;
translations.idiomatic: When Ji's friends were men of distinction, she herself prepared wine and food;

sentences.zh: 有不及己者，輒屏臥不餐，須其悔謝乃食。

translations.literal: when there were those who did not measure up to her standards, she would withdraw to bed and refuse to eat until they repented and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: when they fell short of her standards, she would withdraw to bed and refuse to eat until they repented.

sentences.zh: 善誘嚴訓，類皆如是。

translations.literal: Skilled in gentle guidance and strict instruction, in all matters it was thus.
translations.idiomatic: In gentle guidance and strict discipline alike, she acted thus in every matter.

sentences.zh: 年六十五而終。

translations.literal: At age sixty-five she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 緝事在序傳。

translations.literal: Ji's affairs are recorded in the ordered biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's biography appears elsewhere in this work.

sentences.zh: 緝子悅為濟陰太守，吏民立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Ji's son Yue became Administrator of Jiyin; officials and commoners erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Yue became Administrator of Jiyin, and officials and commoners erected a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫高閭為其文，序云：「祖母房年在弱笄，艱貞守志，秉恭妻之操，著自毀之誠。

translations.literal: Grandee of the Golden Bell and Purple Radiance Gao Lu composed its text; the preface says: "Grandmother Fang, in the years of her tender hairpin, endured hardship and kept her resolve, upholding the conduct of a respectful wife and displaying the sincerity of self-mutilation.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee of the Golden Bell and Purple Radiance Gao Lu composed its inscription, writing in the preface: "Our grandmother Fang, still in her maiden years, bore hardship and held to her resolve, embodying the conduct of a devoted wife and the sincerity of her self-mutilation.

sentences.zh: 」又頌曰：「爰及處士，遘疾夙凋。

translations.literal: " He also composed a eulogy, saying: "Reaching the retired gentleman, he met with illness and perished early.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote a eulogy: "When the retired gentleman fell ill, he perished before his time.

sentences.zh: 伉儷秉志，識茂行高。

translations.literal: The matched pair held to their resolve; in insight they were abundant and in conduct lofty.
translations.idiomatic: The wedded pair held firm to their purpose, rich in understanding and lofty in conduct.

sentences.zh: 殘形顯操，誓敦久要。

translations.literal: Mutilating her form, she displayed her integrity; she vowed to fulfill their long bond.
translations.idiomatic: She maimed her body to show her integrity and vowed to honor their lifelong bond.

sentences.zh: 誕茲令胤，幽感乃昭。

translations.literal: She brought forth this fine heir; hidden feeling was thereby made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: She bore this fine heir, and devotion hidden in the depths was brought to light.

sentences.zh: 」溥未仕而卒，故云處士焉。

translations.literal: " Pu died without having taken office, hence he is called a retired gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: " Pu died without ever taking office, hence he is called a retired gentleman.

sentences.zh: 樂部郎胡長命妻張氏，事姑王氏甚謹。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang, wife of Bureau of Music Gentleman Hu Changming, served her mother-in-law Lady Wang with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, consort of Bureau of Music Gentleman Hu Changming, served her mother-in-law Lady Wang with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 太安中，京師禁酒，張以姑老且患，私為醞之，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era, wine was forbidden in the capital; Zhang, because her mother-in-law was old and ill, privately brewed wine for her and was reported by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era, wine was banned in the capital; because her mother-in-law was old and ill, Zhang brewed wine for her in secret and was reported by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 王氏詣曹自告曰：「老病須酒，在家私釀，王所為也。

translations.literal: Lady Wang went to the office and confessed herself, saying: "In old age and illness wine is needed; the private brewing at home was done by Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang went to the authorities and confessed: "In my old age and illness I need wine; the brewing at home was my doing.

sentences.zh: 」張氏曰：「姑老抱患，張主家事，姑不知釀，其罪在張。

translations.literal: " Lady Zhang said: "My mother-in-law is old and afflicted with illness; Zhang manages the household affairs; my mother-in-law did not know of the brewing—the guilt lies with Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Zhang said, "My mother-in-law is old and ill; I manage the household—she knew nothing of the brewing. The guilt is mine.

sentences.zh: 」主司疑其罪，不知所處。

translations.literal: " The presiding official was uncertain as to their guilt and did not know how to dispose of the case.
translations.idiomatic: " The presiding official could not determine who was guilty and did not know how to rule.

sentences.zh: 平原王陸麗以狀奏，高宗義而赦之。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li memorialized the circumstances; Emperor Gaozong, moved by righteousness, pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li reported the matter to the throne; Emperor Gaozong, moved by their righteousness, pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 平原鄃縣女子孫氏男玉者，夫為靈縣民所殺。

translations.literal: Sun Nanyu, a woman of Suxian in Pingyuan, had a husband who was killed by a man of Ling County.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Nanyu, a woman of Suxian in Pingyuan, had a husband who was murdered by a man from Ling County.

sentences.zh: 追執讎人，男玉欲自殺之，其弟止而不聽。

translations.literal: Pursuing and seizing the enemy, Nanyu wished to kill him herself; her younger brother stopped her but she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the killer in pursuit; Nanyu wished to kill him herself, but her younger brother tried to stop her and she would not listen.

sentences.zh: 男玉曰：「女人出適，以夫為天，當親自復雪，云何假人之手！

translations.literal: Nanyu said: "When a woman goes forth in marriage, she takes her husband as heaven; she ought personally to exact vengeance—how could she borrow another's hand!
translations.idiomatic: Nanyu said, "A woman who marries takes her husband as her heaven; I must avenge him myself—how could I leave it to another's hand!

sentences.zh: 」遂以杖毆殺之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she beat him to death with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: " She then beat him to death with a staff.

sentences.zh: 有司處死以聞。

translations.literal: The authorities sentenced her to death and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities sentenced her to death and reported the case to the throne.

sentences.zh: 顯祖詔曰：「男玉重節輕身，以義犯法，緣情定罪，理在可原，其特恕之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu issued an edict, saying: "Nanyu valued integrity and held life lightly; she violated the law out of righteousness. Considering the circumstances in fixing guilt, reason lies in pardon—she is specially forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu issued an edict: "Nanyu prized integrity above her own life and broke the law in the name of righteousness. Given the circumstances, she deserves mercy—let her be specially pardoned."

sentences.zh: 清河房愛親妻崔氏者，同郡崔元孫之女。

translations.literal: Lady Cui, wife of Fang Aiqin of Qinghe, was a daughter of Cui Yuansun of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui, consort of Fang Aiqin of Qinghe, was the daughter of Cui Yuansun of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 性嚴明高尚，歷覽書傳，多所聞知。

translations.literal: Her nature was stern, clear, lofty, and noble; she had read through books and records and had learned much.
translations.idiomatic: Stern, principled, and of lofty character, she had read widely in books and records and possessed deep learning.

sentences.zh: 子景伯、景先，崔氏親授經義，[7]學行修明，並為當世名士。

translations.literal: Her sons Jingbo and Jingxian—Lady Cui personally taught them the classics; [7] their learning and conduct were cultivated and clear, and both became eminent men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Jingbo and Jingxian received the classics directly from Lady Cui; [7] both became men of cultivated learning and conduct, renowned in their day.

sentences.zh: 景伯為清河太守，每有疑獄，常先請焉。

translations.literal: Jingbo served as Administrator of Qinghe; whenever there was a doubtful legal case, he would first consult her.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingbo served as Administrator of Qinghe, he would consult her first whenever a difficult case arose.

sentences.zh: 貝丘民列子不孝，吏欲案之。

translations.literal: A commoner of Beiqiu named Liezi was unfilial; the clerks wished to prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Beiqiu named Liezi was accused of unfilial conduct, and the clerks wished to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 景伯為之悲傷，入白其母。

translations.literal: Jingbo was grieved for him and went in to report to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo was moved to pity and went to tell his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「吾聞聞不如見，山民未見禮教，何足責哉？

translations.literal: His mother said: "I have heard that hearing is not equal to seeing; mountain folk have not seen ritual teaching—how can they be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "I have heard that hearing is not equal to seeing. These mountain folk have never been taught ritual propriety—how can we blame them?

sentences.zh: 但呼其母來，吾與之同居。

translations.literal: Simply summon his mother here; I shall dwell with her.
translations.idiomatic: Summon his mother here; I shall live with her.

sentences.zh: 其子置汝左右，令其見汝事吾，或應自改。

translations.literal: Place her son at your side and let him see how you serve me; perhaps he will reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: Keep her son at your side and let him watch how you serve me—perhaps he will reform himself.

sentences.zh: 」景伯遂召其母，崔氏處之於榻，與之共食。

translations.literal: " Jingbo then summoned the mother; Lady Cui seated her on a couch and ate with her.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingbo summoned the mother; Lady Cui seated her on a couch and shared meals with her.

sentences.zh: 景伯之溫凊，其子侍立堂下。

translations.literal: As Jingbo attended to her warmth and coolness, the son stood waiting below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: While Jingbo attended to her comfort, the son stood waiting in the hall below.

sentences.zh: 未及旬日，悔過求還。

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed, he repented and asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he repented and asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 崔氏曰：「此雖顏慚，未知心愧，且可置之。

translations.literal: Lady Cui said: "Though his face shows shame, I do not yet know whether his heart feels guilt; for now he may be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui said, "His face shows shame, but I do not yet know whether his heart feels guilt. Let him wait awhile.

sentences.zh: 」凡經二十餘日，其子叩頭流血，其母涕泣乞還，然後聽之，終以孝聞。

translations.literal: " After more than twenty days in all, the son knocked his head until it bled and his mother wept and begged to return; only then did she consent, and in the end he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: " After more than twenty days, the son knocked his head until it bled and his mother wept and begged to take him home; only then did she consent, and he became known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 其識度厲物如此，竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Such was her insight and the sternness with which she admonished others; in the end she died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: Such was her insight and the authority with which she guided others; she lived to a full age.

sentences.zh: 涇州貞女兕先氏，許嫁彭老生為妻，娉幣既畢，未及成禮。

translations.literal: The chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture had been betrothed to Peng Laosheng as his wife; betrothal gifts were complete, but the marriage rites had not yet been performed.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture had been betrothed to Peng Laosheng; the betrothal gifts were complete, but the wedding had not yet taken place.

sentences.zh: 兕先率行貞淑，居貧常自舂汲，以養父母。

translations.literal: Sixian conducted herself with chaste purity; living in poverty she often pounded grain and drew water herself to support her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Sixian conducted herself with chaste purity; though poor, she pounded grain and drew water herself to support her parents.

sentences.zh: 老生輒往逼之，女曰：「與君禮命雖畢，二門多故，未及相見。

translations.literal: Laosheng repeatedly went to force himself upon her; the girl said: "Though ritual obligations between us are complete, both our households have had many troubles and we have not yet met.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng repeatedly tried to force himself upon her; she said, "Though our betrothal is settled, both our families have suffered many troubles and we have not yet met.

sentences.zh: 何由不禀父母，擅見陵辱！

translations.literal: How could you fail to inform our parents and on your own come to insult and violate me!
translations.idiomatic: How dare you come to violate me without informing our parents!

sentences.zh: 若苟行非禮，正可身死耳。

translations.literal: If you rashly act against ritual, I can only die.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on violating propriety, I would rather die.

sentences.zh: 」遂不肯從。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 老生怒而刺殺之，取其衣服。

translations.literal: Laosheng in anger stabbed and killed her and took her clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng in a rage stabbed her to death and took her clothing.

sentences.zh: 女尚能言，臨死謂老生曰：「生身何罪，與君相遇。

translations.literal: The girl could still speak; on the verge of death she said to Laosheng: "What crime did my living body commit, that it should meet you?
translations.idiomatic: She could still speak; dying, she said to Laosheng, "What crime did I commit in being born, that I should meet you?

sentences.zh: 我所以執節自固者，寧更有所邀？

translations.literal: The reason I held to my integrity and stood firm—was it that I sought anything else?
translations.idiomatic: The reason I held firm to my integrity—was it that I sought anything else?

sentences.zh: 正欲奉給君耳。

translations.literal: I simply wished to serve and provide for you.
translations.idiomatic: I wished only to serve you properly.

sentences.zh: 今反為君所殺，若魂靈有知，自當相報。

translations.literal: Now instead I am killed by you; if the soul has awareness, it will surely repay you.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have killed me instead; if spirits have knowledge, they will surely repay you.

sentences.zh: 」言終而絕。

translations.literal: " When her words ended, she expired.
translations.idiomatic: " With these words she died.

sentences.zh: 老生持女珠瓔至其叔宅，以告叔。

translations.literal: Laosheng took the girl's pearl ornaments to her uncle's house and told the uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng took the girl's pearl ornaments to her uncle's house and told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 叔曰：「此是汝婦，奈何殺之，天不祐汝！

translations.literal: The uncle said: "This was your wife—how could you kill her? Heaven will not bless you!
translations.idiomatic: The uncle said, "She was your betrothed—how could you kill her? Heaven will not protect you!

sentences.zh: 」遂執送官。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he seized him and handed him over to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized him and handed him over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 太和七年，有司劾以死罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, the authorities impeached him for the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe, the authorities charged him with a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「老生不仁，侵陵貞淑，原其強暴，便可戮之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Laosheng was without benevolence and violated the chaste and pure; considering his violence and outrage, he may be executed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Laosheng was cruel and violated a chaste woman; given his violence, let him be executed.

sentences.zh: 而女守禮履節，沒身不改，雖處草萊，行合古跡，宜賜美名，以顯風操。

translations.literal: The girl upheld ritual and kept her integrity, unchanged to the end; though she dwelt among common folk, her conduct accorded with ancient exemplars—she should be granted a fine name to display her moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The girl upheld ritual and integrity to the end; though she lived among common folk, her conduct matched the ancients—grant her a fine name to display her virtue.

sentences.zh: 其標墓旌善，號曰『貞女』。」

translations.literal: Mark her tomb and proclaim her goodness, styling her the 'Chaste Woman.'"
translations.idiomatic: Mark her tomb and proclaim her virtue, styling her the 'Chaste Woman.'"

sentences.zh: 姚氏婦楊氏者，閹人苻承祖姨也。

translations.literal: Lady Yang, daughter-in-law of the Yao clan, was the aunt of the eunuch Fu Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang of the Yao household was the aunt of the eunuch Fu Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 家貧無產業。

translations.literal: Her family was poor and without property.
translations.idiomatic: Her family was poor and owned no property.

sentences.zh: 及承祖為文明太后所寵貴，親姻皆求利潤，唯楊獨不欲。

translations.literal: When Chengzu came to be favored and ennobled by Empress Dowager Wenming, relatives by marriage all sought profit—only Yang did not wish it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu won favor and rank from Empress Dowager Wenming, all his kin by marriage sought profit—only Yang refused.

sentences.zh: 常謂其姊曰：「姊雖有一時之榮，不若妹有無憂之樂。

translations.literal: She often said to her elder sister: "Sister, though you have momentary glory, it is not equal to my younger sister's carefree joy.
translations.idiomatic: She often told her elder sister, "Sister, your momentary glory is nothing beside my carefree peace.

sentences.zh: 」姊每遺其衣服，多不受，強與之，則云：「我夫家世貧，好衣美服，則使人不安。

translations.literal: " Whenever her sister sent her clothing, she mostly would not accept it; if forced to take it, she would say: "My husband's family has been poor for generations; fine clothes and beautiful garments make people uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: " When her sister sent her clothing, she usually refused it; if pressed to accept, she said, "My husband's family has been poor for generations—fine clothes would make us uneasy.

sentences.zh: 」與之奴婢，則云：「我家無食，不能供給。

translations.literal: " When given maidservants, she would say: "My household has no food and cannot support them.
translations.idiomatic: " When given servants, she said, "We have no food at home and cannot support them.

sentences.zh: 」終不肯受。

translations.literal: " In the end she would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end she would accept nothing.

sentences.zh: 常著破衣，自執勞事。

translations.literal: She constantly wore worn clothing and performed labor herself.
translations.idiomatic: She wore worn clothing and performed labor with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 時受其衣服，多不著，密埋之，設有著者，污之而後服。

translations.literal: When she did accept clothing, she mostly would not wear it, burying it in secret; if she did wear any, she would soil it first and then put it on.
translations.idiomatic: When she did accept clothing, she rarely wore it, burying it in secret; if she wore any at all, she soiled it first.

sentences.zh: 承祖每見其寒悴，深恨其母，謂不供給之。

translations.literal: Whenever Chengzu saw her pallid with cold, he deeply resented his mother, saying she did not provide for her.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chengzu saw her thin and shivering with cold, he blamed his mother for not providing for her.

sentences.zh: 乃啟其母曰：「今承祖一身何所乏少，而使姨如是？

translations.literal: He then reported to his mother: "Now that Chengzu himself lacks for nothing, why should my aunt be thus?
translations.idiomatic: He told his mother, "I myself lack for nothing now—why should my aunt live like this?

sentences.zh: 」母具以語之。

translations.literal: " His mother told him the full story.
translations.idiomatic: " His mother told him the full story.

sentences.zh: 承祖乃遣人乘車往迎之，則厲志不起，遣人強舁於車上，則大哭，言：「爾欲殺我也！

translations.literal: Chengzu then sent men in a carriage to fetch her, but her resolve was firm and she would not rise; when men forcibly lifted her into the carriage, she wept loudly, saying: "You wish to kill me!
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu sent men in a carriage to fetch her, but her resolve was firm and she would not go; when they forced her into the carriage, she wept and cried, "You mean to kill me!

sentences.zh: 」由是苻家內外皆號為癡姨。

translations.literal: " From this, within and without the Fu household all called her the mad aunt.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on, everyone in the Fu household called her the mad aunt.

sentences.zh: 及承祖敗，有司執其二姨至殿庭。

translations.literal: When Chengzu fell, the authorities seized his two aunts and brought them to the palace court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu fell from power, the authorities seized both his aunts and brought them before the throne.

sentences.zh: 一姨致法，以姚氏婦衣裳弊陋，特免其罪。

translations.literal: One aunt was punished by law; because the Yao clan daughter-in-law's clothing was worn and shabby, her guilt was specially remitted.
translations.idiomatic: One aunt was punished; because the Yao daughter-in-law's clothing was worn and shabby, her guilt was specially remitted.

sentences.zh: 其識機雖呂嬃亦不過也。

translations.literal: Her discernment of opportunity—even Lü Hou could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Her foresight—even Empress Lü could not have surpassed it.

sentences.zh: 滎陽京縣人張洪初妻劉氏，年十七，夫亡，遺腹生子，三歲又沒。

translations.literal: Lady Liu, wife of Zhang Hongchu of Jing County in Xingyang, was seventeen when her husband died; she bore a posthumous son, who died at age three.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, consort of Zhang Hongchu of Jing County in Xingyang, was seventeen when her husband died; she bore a posthumous son who died at age three.

sentences.zh: 其舅姑年老，朝夕奉養，率禮無違。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law were old; morning and evening she provided for them, observing ritual without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law were elderly; morning and evening she cared for them, observing every propriety.

sentences.zh: 兄矜其少寡，欲奪而嫁之。

translations.literal: Her elder brother pitied her youth and widowhood and wished to take her away and marry her off.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother pitied her youth and widowhood and wished to marry her off again.

sentences.zh: 劉氏自誓弗許，以終其身。

translations.literal: Lady Liu vowed herself and would not consent, remaining so to the end of her life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu vowed never to consent and remained a widow for life.

sentences.zh: 陳留董景起妻張氏。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang, wife of Dong Jingqi of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, consort of Dong Jingqi of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 景起早亡，張時年十六，痛夫少喪，哀傷過禮。

translations.literal: Jingqi died early; Zhang was then sixteen, grieving that her husband died young, her mourning exceeding ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqi died young; Zhang was then sixteen and mourned her husband's early death with grief beyond what ritual required.

sentences.zh: 形容毀頓，永不沐浴，蔬食長齋。

translations.literal: Her appearance was wasted and broken; she never bathed, ate vegetables, and kept long fasts.
translations.idiomatic: Her appearance wasted away; she never bathed, ate only vegetables, and kept perpetual fasts.

sentences.zh: 又無兒息，獨守貞操，期以闔棺。

translations.literal: Moreover she had no children; alone she kept chaste integrity, expecting to share the coffin at the close.
translations.idiomatic: She had no children and held to chaste integrity alone, resolved to share his coffin at the end.

sentences.zh: 鄉曲高之，終見標異。

translations.literal: The neighborhood held her in esteem; in the end she was marked out as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Her neighbors held her in high esteem, and in the end she was publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 漁陽太守陽尼妻高氏，勃海人。

translations.literal: Lady Gao, wife of Yang Ni, Administrator of Yuyang, was a native of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao, consort of Yang Ni, Administrator of Yuyang, was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 學識有文才，高祖敕令入侍後宮。

translations.literal: Learned and accomplished, with literary talent, Emperor Gaozu ordered her to attend in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and gifted with literary talent, Emperor Gaozu ordered her to serve in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 幽后表啟，悉其辭也。

translations.literal: The memorials and reports of Empress You were entirely in her wording.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials and reports of Empress You were entirely composed by her.

sentences.zh: 滎陽史映周妻同郡耿氏女，年十七，適於映周。

translations.literal: Lady Geng, wife of Shi Yingzhou of Xingyang, was a daughter of the Geng clan of the same commandery; at seventeen she was married to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Geng, consort of Shi Yingzhou of Xingyang, was a daughter of the Geng clan of the same commandery; at seventeen she married Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太和二十三年，映周卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe, Yingzhou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Taihe, Yingzhou died.

sentences.zh: 耿氏恐父母奪其志，因葬映周，哀哭而殯。

translations.literal: Lady Geng feared her parents would wrest away her resolve; as Yingzhou was buried, she mourned and wept beside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Geng feared her parents would force her to remarry; as Yingzhou was buried, she wept beside his coffin.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不悲歎。

translations.literal: All who saw were moved to grief and lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 屬大使觀風，以狀具上，詔標牓門閭。

translations.literal: When an envoy came to observe local customs, the circumstances were fully reported upward; an edict marked her gate and lane with honor.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy came to observe local customs, her case was reported to the throne; an edict ordered her gate and lane marked with honor.

sentences.zh: 任城國太妃孟氏，鉅鹿人，尚書令、任城王澄之母。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Meng of the State of Rencheng was a native of Julu and mother of Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Meng of Rencheng was a native of Julu and mother of Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Rencheng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄為揚州之日，率眾出討。

translations.literal: When Cheng was in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng served in Yangzhou, he led troops out on campaign.

sentences.zh: 於後賊帥姜慶真陰結逆黨，襲陷羅城。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandit chief Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined rebellious factions and in a surprise attack seized Luocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the rebel leader Jiang Qingzhen secretly joined traitors and seized Luocheng in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 長史韋纘倉卒失圖，計無所出。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan in the emergency lost his plan and had no course to take.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was caught unprepared and could think of no plan.

sentences.zh: 孟乃勒兵登陴，先守要便。

translations.literal: Meng then marshaled troops onto the battlements and first secured the strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Meng then rallied the troops onto the battlements and secured the strategic points.

sentences.zh: 激厲文武，安慰新舊，勸以賞罰，喻之逆順，於是咸有奮志。

translations.literal: She roused civil and military officers, comforted old and new alike, urged them with rewards and punishments, and instructed them in loyalty and rebellion; thereby all were stirred to resolve.
translations.idiomatic: She roused the civil and military officers, comforted old and new alike, urged them with rewards and punishments, and taught them the difference between loyalty and treason; all were stirred to fight.

sentences.zh: 親自巡守，不避矢石。

translations.literal: She personally made the rounds on guard, not avoiding arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: She personally made the rounds on the walls, heedless of arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 賊不能克，卒以全城。

translations.literal: The rebels could not overcome them and in the end the whole city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could not take the city, and the whole fortress was preserved.

sentences.zh: 澄以狀表聞，屬世宗崩，[8]事寢。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized the circumstances; as it happened Emperor Shizong died, [8] and the matter was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng reported the matter to the throne, but Emperor Shizong died [8] and the matter was set aside.

sentences.zh: 靈太后後令曰：「鴻功盛美，實宜垂之永年。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered: "Great merit and splendid virtue truly ought to be handed down through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling later ordered: "Such great merit and splendid virtue ought to be handed down through the ages.

sentences.zh: 」乃敕有司樹碑旌美。

translations.literal: " She then ordered the authorities to erect a stele proclaiming her excellence.
translations.idiomatic: " She then ordered the authorities to erect a stele in her honor.

sentences.zh: 苟金龍妻劉氏，平原人也。

translations.literal: Lady Liu, wife of Gou Jinlong, was a native of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, consort of Gou Jinlong, was a native of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 廷尉少卿劉叔宗之姊。

translations.literal: She was the elder sister of Vice Director of Justice Liu Shuzong.
translations.idiomatic: She was the elder sister of Vice Director of Justice Liu Shuzong.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，金龍為梓潼太守，郡帶關城戍主。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong, Jinlong was Administrator of Zitong; the commandery included Guancheng, where he was garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's reign, Jinlong served as Administrator of Zitong and commander of the garrison at Guancheng.

sentences.zh: [9]蕭衍遣眾攻圍，值金龍疾病，不堪部分，眾甚危懼。

translations.literal: [9] Xiao Yan sent troops to attack and besiege them; as it happened Jinlong was ill and unable to deploy forces—the troops were greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Xiao Yan sent troops to besiege the city; Jinlong fell ill and could not command—the garrison was gripped with fear.

sentences.zh: 劉遂率厲城民，修理戰具，一夜悉成。

translations.literal: Liu then led and encouraged the city folk, repaired war equipment, and in one night all was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu rallied the townspeople, repaired the weapons of war, and finished everything in a single night.

sentences.zh: 拒戰百有餘日，兵士死傷過半。

translations.literal: They resisted battle for more than a hundred days; soldiers killed and wounded exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: They held out for more than a hundred days; more than half the soldiers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 戍副高景陰圖叛逆，劉斬之，及其黨與數十人。

translations.literal: Deputy garrison commander Gao Jing secretly plotted rebellion; Liu beheaded him along with several tens of his associates.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Gao Jing secretly plotted treason; Liu beheaded him and several dozen of his followers.

sentences.zh: 自餘將士，分衣減食，勞逸必同，莫不畏而懷之。

translations.literal: As for the remaining officers and soldiers, she divided clothing and reduced rations, sharing hardship and ease alike; none failed to revere and embrace her.
translations.idiomatic: She shared clothing and reduced rations among the remaining troops, sharing hardship and ease alike; all revered and embraced her.

sentences.zh: 井在外城，尋為賊陷，城中絕水，渴死者多。

translations.literal: The wells lay outside the outer wall and soon fell to the rebels; within the city water was cut off and many died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The wells lay outside the outer wall and soon fell to the enemy; water inside the city ran out and many died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 劉乃集諸長幼，喻以忠節，遂相率告訴於天，俱時號叫，俄而澍雨。

translations.literal: Liu then gathered elders and young, instructed them in loyalty and integrity, and they together appealed to Heaven, all crying out at once; shortly afterward a soaking rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liu gathered young and old, taught them loyalty and integrity, and led them in crying out to Heaven together; shortly afterward a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 劉命出公私布絹及至衣服，懸之城中，絞而取水，所有雜器悉儲之。

translations.literal: Liu ordered public and private cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, wrung to draw water, and all miscellaneous vessels stored for the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Liu ordered cloth, silk, and even clothing brought out, hung within the city, and wrung for water; every vessel was put to use.

sentences.zh: 於是人心益固。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people's hearts grew firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: The people's resolve grew firmer still.

sentences.zh: 會益州刺史傅豎眼將至，賊乃退散。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was about to arrive, and the rebels then dispersed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Inspector of Yizhou Fu Shuyan was approaching, and the enemy dispersed.

sentences.zh: 豎眼歎異，具狀奏聞，世宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Shuyan marveled and reported the full circumstances; Emperor Shizong commended her.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan marveled at her deeds and reported them to the throne; Emperor Shizong praised her.

sentences.zh: 正光中，賞平昌縣開國子，邑二百戶，授子慶珍，又得二子出身。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, she was rewarded with the title Viscount of Pingchang County, fief of two hundred households, granted to her son Qingzhen, and two sons additionally received entry into office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era, her son Qingzhen was granted the title Viscount of Pingchang with a fief of two hundred households, and two other sons received entry into office.

sentences.zh: 慶珍卒，子純陀襲。

translations.literal: Qingzhen died; his son Chuntuo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhen died, his son Chuntuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 慶珍弟孚，武定末，儀同開府司馬。

translations.literal: Qingzhen's younger brother Fu, at the end of Wuding, was Chief Clerk of the Equal in Attendance Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhen's younger brother Fu, at the end of Wuding, served as Chief Clerk of the Equal in Attendance Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 貞孝女宗者，趙郡栢仁人，趙郡太守李叔胤之女，范陽盧元禮之妻。

translations.literal: The filial and chaste woman Zong was a native of Boren in Zhao Commandery, daughter of Administrator of Zhao Li Shuyin, and wife of Lu Yuanli of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The filial and chaste woman Zong was a native of Boren in Zhao Commandery, daughter of Administrator of Zhao Li Shuyin, and consort of Lu Yuanli of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，聞於州里。

translations.literal: Her nature was supremely filial, renowned throughout the commandery and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned throughout her commandery for supreme filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 父卒，號慟幾絕者數四，賴母崔氏慰勉之，得全。

translations.literal: When her father died, she cried and wailed until nearly expiring four times; relying on her mother Lady Cui's comfort and encouragement, she survived.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died, she wailed until she nearly expired four times; only her mother Lady Cui's comfort saved her.

sentences.zh: 三年之中，形骸銷瘠，非人扶不起。

translations.literal: Throughout the three years, her body wasted away; without someone to support her she could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: For three years her body wasted away; she could not rise without support.

sentences.zh: 及歸夫氏，與母分隔，便飲食日損，涕泣不絕，日就羸篤。

translations.literal: When she returned to her husband's clan and was separated from her mother, her food and drink daily diminished, her weeping never ceased, and day by day she grew frail and grave.
translations.idiomatic: When she joined her husband's household and was separated from her mother, she ate less each day, wept without cease, and grew steadily weaker.

sentences.zh: 盧氏合家慰喻，不解，乃遣歸寧。

translations.literal: The whole Lu household comforted and admonished her without effect, and then sent her home for a visit.
translations.idiomatic: The entire Lu household tried in vain to console her and sent her home for a visit.

sentences.zh: 還家乃復故，如此者八九焉。

translations.literal: Returning home she would recover as before; this happened eight or nine times.
translations.idiomatic: At home she would recover, only to decline again when she returned—this happened eight or nine times.

sentences.zh: 後元禮卒，李追亡撫存，禮無違者，事姑以孝謹著。

translations.literal: Later Yuanli died; Li pursued the departed and cared for the living, observing ritual without violation, and became known for serving her mother-in-law with filial care and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanli died, Zong mourned him and cared for the living with scrupulous observance of ritual, becoming known for devoted service to her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 母崔，以神龜元年終於洛陽，凶問初到，舉聲慟絕，一宿乃蘇，水漿不入口者六日。

translations.literal: Her mother Cui died in Luoyang in the first year of Shengui; when the news of death first arrived, she raised her voice in grief and expired, reviving only after one night; for six days she took no water or food.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Cui died in Luoyang in the first year of Shengui; when the news arrived, Zong cried out and collapsed, reviving only after a night; for six days she took no food or water.

sentences.zh: 其姑慮其不濟，親送奔喪。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law feared she would not survive and personally escorted her to rush to the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing she would not survive the journey, her mother-in-law personally escorted her to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 而氣力危殆，自范陽向洛，八旬方達，攀櫬號踴，遂卒。

translations.literal: But her strength was perilously weak; from Fanyang toward Luoyang, eighty days were required to arrive; clinging to the coffin she wailed and stamped, and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: Her strength failing, she took eighty days to travel from Fanyang to Luoyang; clinging to her mother's coffin, she wailed and stamped—and died.

sentences.zh: 有司以狀聞。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported her case to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「孔子稱毀不滅性，蓋為其廢養絕類也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Confucius said that self-injury must not destroy one's nature—this was because it abandons nurturing and cuts off one's kind.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Confucius said that grief must not destroy one's nature, for excessive mourning abandons the living and cuts off one's line.

sentences.zh: 李既非嫡子，而孝不勝哀，雖乖俯就，而志厲義遠，若不加旌異，則無以勸引澆浮。

translations.literal: Though Li was not a legitimate son, her filial piety could not overcome grief; though she departed from yielding compliance, her resolve was stern and her righteousness far-reaching—if she is not specially honored, there will be no means to encourage and guide the shallow and drifting.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zong was not a legitimate heir, her filial devotion overcame all bounds; though she failed to preserve her life, her resolve was fierce and her righteousness profound. Without special honor, how may we guide those adrift in shallow ways?

sentences.zh: 可追號曰『貞孝女宗』，易其里為孝德里，標李盧二門，以惇風俗。」

translations.literal: She may be posthumously styled the 'Filial and Chaste Woman Zong,' her lane changed to Filial Virtue Lane, and the Li and Lu households marked out to enrich custom."
translations.idiomatic: Let her be posthumously styled the 'Filial and Chaste Woman Zong,' her lane renamed Filial Virtue Lane, and the Li and Lu households honored to enrich the customs of the realm."

sentences.zh: 河東姚氏女字女勝，少喪父，無兄弟，母憐而守養。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Yao clan of Hedong, styled Nüsheng, lost her father young; having no brothers, her mother pitied and kept her to rear.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the Yao clan of Hedong, styled Nüsheng, lost her father in childhood; having no brothers, her mother kept and reared her alone.

sentences.zh: 年六七歲，便有孝性，人言其父者，聞輒垂泣。

translations.literal: At six or seven years she already possessed filial nature; whenever people spoke of her father, upon hearing she would weep.
translations.idiomatic: At six or seven she already showed filial feeling; whenever anyone spoke of her father, she wept.

sentences.zh: 隣伍異之。

translations.literal: Neighbors and wards found it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Her neighbors marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 正光中，母死，女勝年十五，哭泣不絕聲，水漿不入口者數日，不勝哀，遂死。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era her mother died; Nüsheng was fifteen, weeping without cease, taking no water or food for several days; unable to bear grief, she died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era her mother died; Nüsheng was fifteen and wept without cease, taking no food or water for days; overcome by grief, she died.

sentences.zh: 太守崔游申請為營墓立碑，自為製文，表其門閭，比之曹娥，改其里曰上虞里。

translations.literal: Administrator Cui You petitioned to build her tomb and erect a stele, composing the text himself, marking her gate and lane, comparing her to Cao E, and changing her lane to Shangyu Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Cui You petitioned to build her tomb and erect a stele, composing the inscription himself, honoring her gate and lane, comparing her to Cao E, and renaming her lane Shangyu Lane.

sentences.zh: 墓在郡城東六里大道北，至今名為孝女冢。

translations.literal: Her tomb lies six li east of the commandery seat on the north side of the great road; to this day it is called the Tomb of the Filial Daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her tomb lies six li east of the commandery seat on the north side of the main road; to this day it is called the Tomb of the Filial Daughter.

sentences.zh: 滎陽刁思遵妻，魯氏女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Diao Sizun of Xingyang was a daughter of the Lu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Diao Sizun of Xingyang was a daughter of the Lu clan.

sentences.zh: 始笄，為思遵所娉，未踰月而思遵亡。

translations.literal: Just upon pinning up her hair, she was betrothed to Sizun; before a month had passed Sizun died.
translations.idiomatic: Just as she came of age, she was betrothed to Sizun; before a month had passed, he died.

sentences.zh: 其家矜其少寡，許嫁已定，魯聞之，以死自誓。

translations.literal: His family pitied her youth and widowhood; a betrothal for remarriage was settled; when Lu heard of it, she vowed herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: His family pitied her youth and arranged another marriage; when Lu heard of it, she vowed to die rather than remarry.

sentences.zh: 父母不達其志，遂經郡訴，稱刁氏吝護寡女，不使歸寧。

translations.literal: Her parents did not understand her resolve and appealed through the commandery, claiming the Diao clan was stingy and protective of the young widow, not allowing her to return home for visits.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents did not understand her purpose and appealed to the commandery, claiming the Diao clan was keeping the young widow from visiting her parents.

sentences.zh: 魯乃與老姑徒步詣司徒府，自告情狀。

translations.literal: Lu then walked on foot with her aged mother-in-law to the Secretariat Director's office and reported the circumstances herself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu then walked on foot with her aged mother-in-law to the Secretariat and reported the truth herself.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，有司聞奏，廢帝詔曰：「貞夫節婦，古今同尚，可令本司依式標牓。」

translations.literal: In the early Putai era the authorities reported it; Emperor Fei issued an edict: "Chaste husbands and principled wives are honored alike in ancient and modern times—let this office mark her gate according to precedent."
translations.idiomatic: In the early Putai era the authorities reported the case; Emperor Fei decreed: "Chaste husbands and faithful wives have been honored in every age—let this office mark her gate according to precedent."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰。

translations.literal: The historian says:
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks:

translations.literal: 〈Missing〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Missing〉

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 涇州貞女兕先氏 北史卷九一傳目及傳「兕先」作「兒」。

translations.literal: The chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture: in the table of contents and biography of juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "Sixian" is written as "Er."
translations.idiomatic: The chaste woman Sixian of Jing Prefecture: in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, both the table of contents and the biography read "Er" instead of "Sixian."

sentences.zh: 張洪初妻劉氏 北史卷九一傳目及傳「初」作「祁」。

translations.literal: Lady Liu, wife of Zhang Hongchu: in the table of contents and biography of juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "Chu" is written as "Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, consort of Zhang Hongchu: in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, both the table of contents and the biography read "Qi" instead of "Chu."

sentences.zh: 魏書卷九十二 諸本目錄此卷注「不全」，卷末有宋人校語云：「此傳雖差多於北史、小史，然亦不完。

translations.literal: Weishu juan 92: in the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked "incomplete"; at the end of the juan there is a Song-dynasty collation note saying: "This biography, though somewhat fuller than in the Northern History and the Minor History, is still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Weishu juan 92: various edition catalogues mark this juan as "incomplete"; a Song-dynasty collation note at the end of the juan reads: "This biography, though somewhat fuller than in the Northern History and the Minor History, is still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「魏收書不全。」

translations.literal: " The textual verification of the Palace Edition says: "Wei Shou's book is incomplete."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Edition's textual verification notes: "Wei Shou's book is incomplete."

sentences.zh: 所以抱怨於黃墟耳 北史卷九一魏溥妻房氏傳「墟」作「壚」。

translations.literal: "This is why I lodge my complaint in the yellow mound": in the biography of Wei Pu's wife Lady Fang in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "mound" is written as "barrow."
translations.idiomatic: "This is why I lodge my complaint in the yellow mound": in the biography of Wei Pu's wife Lady Fang in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "mound (xu)" appears as "barrow (lu)."

sentences.zh: 按「黃壚」見淮南子兵略篇，即黃泉。

translations.literal: Note: "yellow barrow" appears in the Military Strategy chapter of the Huainanzi and means the yellow springs.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Yellow barrow" appears in the Military Strategy chapter of the Huainanzi and means the underworld.

sentences.zh: 「黃墟」不知所出，疑「墟」字訛。

translations.literal: "Yellow mound" has no known source; "mound" is suspected to be a corrupt character.
translations.idiomatic: "Yellow mound" has no known source; "mound (xu)" is likely a corrupt reading.

sentences.zh: 顧當以身少相感長往之恨 北史卷九一「長往」上有「永深」二字，疑此脫，但「相感」屬下讀亦可通，今不補。

translations.literal: "Considering that I am younger, share in the long grief of your departure": in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties there are the two characters "ever deep" above "long departure," suspected to be omitted here, but reading "share in" with what follows is also intelligible—no supplementation is made.
translations.idiomatic: "Considering that I am younger, share in the long grief of your departure": juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties has "ever deep" before "long departure," possibly omitted here, but the text reads coherently without it—no supplementation is made.

sentences.zh: 新婦少年不幸 北史卷九一「不幸」下有「早寡」二字，疑此脫，但無亦通，今不補。

translations.literal: "The new bride met misfortune in her youth": in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties there are the two characters "early widowhood" below "misfortune," suspected to be omitted here, but the text is intelligible without them—no supplementation is made.
translations.idiomatic: "Your daughter-in-law met misfortune young": juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties adds "early widowhood" after "misfortune," possibly omitted here, but the text reads well without it—no supplementation is made.

sentences.zh: 子景伯景先崔氏親授經義 諸本及北史卷九一房愛親妻崔氏傳「景先」作「景光」。

translations.literal: "Her sons Jingbo and Jingxian—Lady Cui personally taught them the classics": in various editions and the biography of Fang Aiqin's wife Lady Cui in juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, "Jingxian" is written as "Jingguang."
translations.idiomatic: "Her sons Jingbo and Jingxian received the classics from Lady Cui": various editions and juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties read "Jingguang" instead of "Jingxian."

sentences.zh: 按卷四三房法壽傳附景伯景先傳，景先傳云：「其母自授毛詩、曲禮。

translations.literal: Note: attached to the biography of Fang Fashou in juan 43 are biographies of Jingbo and Jingxian; the biography of Jingxian says: "His mother personally taught him the Mao Odes and the Record of Rites in One Volume.
translations.idiomatic: Note: juan 43's biography of Fang Fashou includes biographies of Jingbo and Jingxian; Jingxian's biography states: "His mother personally taught him the Mao Odes and the Record of Rites in One Volume.

sentences.zh: 」與此傳合。

translations.literal: " This agrees with this biography.
translations.idiomatic: " This agrees with the present biography.

sentences.zh: 「光」乃「先」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Guang" is a corruption of "xian"; it is corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: "Guang" is a corruption of "xian"; the text is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 屬世宗崩 諸本「宗」作「祖」。

translations.literal: "As it happened Emperor Shizong died": in various editions "Shizong" is written as "Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: "As it happened Emperor Shizong died": various editions read "Ancestor" instead of "Shizong."

sentences.zh: 按卷八世宗紀事在正始元年二月，「祖」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Note: the annals of Emperor Shizong in juan 8 place the event in the second month of the first year of Zhengshi; "Ancestor" is a corrupt character and is corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: Note: juan 8's annals of Emperor Shizong date the event to the second month of the first year of Zhengshi; "Ancestor" is a corrupt reading and is corrected here.

sentences.zh: 金龍為梓潼太守郡帶關城戍主 張森楷云：「『郡』字衍。

translations.literal: "Jinlong was Administrator of Zitong; the commandery included Guancheng garrison commander": Zhang Senkai says: "The character 'commandery' is superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: "Jinlong was Administrator of Zitong, commander of the garrison at Guancheng": Zhang Senkai notes: "The character for 'commandery' is superfluous.

sentences.zh: 」按北史卷九一此傳首稱「梓潼太守苟金龍妻劉氏」，下云「金龍為郡，帶關城戍主」。

translations.literal: " Note: juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties opens this biography with "Lady Liu, wife of Gou Jinlong, Administrator of Zitong," and below says "Jinlong held the commandery and was garrison commander at Guancheng."
translations.idiomatic: " Note: juan 91 of the History of the Northern Dynasties opens this biography with "Lady Liu, consort of Gou Jinlong, Administrator of Zitong," and below reads "Jinlong held office in the commandery as garrison commander at Guancheng."

sentences.zh: 「為郡」即「為太守」。

translations.literal: "Held the commandery" means "served as administrator."
translations.idiomatic: "Held the commandery" means "served as administrator."

sentences.zh: 本書諸傳凡其夫有官者，大都首標官位，如「中書侍郎清河崔覽妻」，「樂部郎胡長命妻」等。

translations.literal: In the biographies of this book, whenever the husband held office, the opening generally gives his title, as in "wife of Cui Lan, Secretariat Gentleman of Qinghe," "wife of Hu Changming, Bureau of Music Gentleman," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: In this book's biographies, when the husband held office, his title usually appears at the opening, as in "consort of Cui Lan, Secretariat Gentleman of Qinghe" and "consort of Hu Changming, Bureau of Music Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 這裏恐本同北史，首稱「梓潼太守苟金龍妻」，「梓潼太守」四字錯簡在此，或後人移易，忘刪「郡」字。

translations.literal: Here it is feared the original text agreed with the Northern History, opening with "wife of Gou Jinlong, Administrator of Zitong"; the four characters "Administrator of Zitong" were misplaced here, or later persons rearranged the text and forgot to delete the character "commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The original text likely agreed with the Northern History, opening with "consort of Gou Jinlong, Administrator of Zitong"; the four characters "Administrator of Zitong" were probably misplaced here, or a later editor rearranged the text and forgot to delete the superfluous "commandery."
